items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: Duke and I are great friends.

ctx.x: What about Duke Ellington? You know him personally?

Well sure. Duke and I are great friends. How'd that happen? Well, through Bonnie. Through Bonnie Biggore, my cousin. When they booked the tour in Texas, I wired Bonnie that I was there and I wanted them to be my guests at my house. So I met them in Austin, Texas, which is 75 miles from San Antonio and then I brought them into San Antonio. By the same token, cab the same way. In those days they had what they called the circuit where they played all of these theater dates. That's most of the dates that Ellington…
When did they have that flood there?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] He's a bass player with Duke Ellington.

ctx.x: He's a bass player with Duke Ellington.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: You take like Blanton that was with Duke that died so young

ctx.x: You take like Blanton that was with Duke that died so young, well Blanton could make his bass sound like a shallow. And those are the things that a lot of musicians don't know how to get tonations out of their horns. You know the smart playing. It's not what we call a pinch tone, it's a round tone, it's big. And a lot of musicians in those days, the first thing they did, they studied their tonations. Like Big Al Loy, Lil Nelson, beautiful tone. Piku, tonation. Or listen to Bonnie's tone.
Well a lot of guys had to work in the street and I think that you have to develop strength and tone and everything there.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: Because we went down there for an audition when Duke was playing in there.

ctx.x: Do you know whether Charlie Johnson was still playing around New York then or not?
Charlie Johnson, I can't recall the name. But I know that the Cotton Club was then on 147 in Lenox. Because we went down there for an audition when Duke was playing in there.
Did you play maybe Small's Paradise? Yeah, that's right.
